text:
This looks like late 2015 to early 2016. Unemployment is 5.1%, which fits around August or September 2015. The fed funds rate is 0.13%, so the Fed had not yet hiked, which means before December 2015. VIX at 26.83 fits the late-August to September 2015 spike. The dollar is up 14% YoY, and emerging-market equities are down sharply, both consistent with 2015. The 10-year yield at 2.05% fits September 2015 (about 2.04%).

Within that window, the 3-month equity return of -7.2% and the VIX of 26.83 fit end of September 2015 better than August. August's one-month return was about -6%, while September's was about -2.6%, which matches the 1m figure. Unemployment was 5.1% in August 2015 and 5.0% in September. At the end of September the latest published value would be the August report, 5.1%. Payrolls averaged about 221k, which also fits.

Headline CPI at 0.22% YoY matches the August 2015 figure of 0.2%.

So the snapshot is September 2015.
